<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,

output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.

n_rows(Nr) :- Nr = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(Nc) :- Nc = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

out_cols(Oc) :- Oc = Nc.

BR1 + BC1 <= BR2 + BC2.

offset1 = BR1 + BC1.
offset2 = BR2 + BC2.
diff    = offset2 - offset1.               % diff ≥ 0 because of the ordering above
Dtemp   = diff * 2.                         % Dtemp = 2·diff

% 3. Choose the period D.
% If offset2 is even we use D = Dtemp‑2, otherwise D = Dtemp.
offset2_even(Kpar) :- offset2 = 2 * Kpar.   % Kpar is an integer, so offset2 is even
% Two mutually exclusive choices for D
1 { D = Dtemp }           1 :- not offset2_even(0).
1 { D = Dtemp - 2 }       1 :- offset2_even(0).

orientation_is_row    :- not orientation_is_column.   % all other non‑zeros must be in column 0

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% 1. Dimensions of the input grid
n_rows(Nr) :- Nr = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(Nc) :- Nc = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output dimensions: one row less than the input and the same number of columns
out_rows(OR) :- OR = Nr - 1.
out_cols(Oc) :- Oc = Nc.

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% 2. Identify the two non‑zero cells (they are assumed to be exactly two)
input(BR1, BC1, V1), V1 != 0.
input(BR2, BC2, V2), V2 != 0,
BR1 != BR2, BC1 != BC2,
BR1 + BC1 <= BR2 + BC2.

% Offsets (the sum of row‑ and column‑indices) and their difference
offset1 = BR1 + BC1.
offset2 = BR2 + BC2.
diff    = offset2 - offset1.               % diff ≥ 0 because of the ordering above
Dtemp   = diff * 2.                         % Dtemp = 2·diff

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% 3. Choose the period D.
% If offset2 is even we use D = Dtemp‑2, otherwise D = Dtemp.
offset2_even(Kpar) :- offset2 = 2 * Kpar.   % Kpar is an integer, so offset2 is even
% Two mutually exclusive choices for D
1 { D = Dtemp }           1 :- not offset2_even(0).
1 { D = Dtemp - 2 }       1 :- offset2_even(0).

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% 4. Orientation: column‑oriented if the first non‑zero cell is not in column 0,
% otherwise row‑oriented.
orientation_is_column :- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0, BC != 0.
orientation_is_row    :- not orientation_is_column.   % all other non‑zeros must be in column 0

% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
% 5. Position conditions for the two values.
% Column‑oriented case (use column % D)
output_cell(R_out, C_out, V1) :- orientation_is_column,
    C_out = D * K + offset1, 
    K >= 0, K < 1000, C_out < out_cols(Oc),
    input(BR1, BC1, V1), V1 != 0.
output_cell(R_out, C_out, V2) :- orientation_is_column,
    C_out = D * K + offset2, 
    K >= 0, K < 1000, C_out < out_cols(Oc),
    input(BR2, BC2, V2), V2 != 0.
output_cell(R_out, C_out, 0) :- orientation_is_column,
    not (C_out = D * K + offset1) or not (C_out = D * K + offset2),
    orientation_is_column,
    input(BR1, BC1, V1), V1 != 0.

% Row‑oriented case (use row % D)
output_cell(R_out, C_out, V1) :- not orientation_is_column,
    R_out = D * K + offset1,

The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-

% Determine rows and columns
n_rows(Nr) :- Nr = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(Nc) :- Nc = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Exactly two non‑zero cells
input(BR1, BC1, V1), V1 != 0.
input(BR2, BC2, V2), V2 != 0,
BR1 != BR2, BC1 != BC2.

% No other non‑zero cells
:- input(R, C, V), V != 0,
    R != BR1, C != BC1,
    R != BR2, C != BC2.

% Determine orientation (column if first non‑zero column ≠ 0)
orientation_is_column :- BC1 != 0, BC1 < BC2.
orientation_is_row    :- not orientation_is_column,
                       BR1 < BR2.

% For column orientation compute D = (BC2 - BC1) + 2
% For row orientation compute D = (BR2 - BR1) + 2

% Output cell for first non‑zero value (V1)
output_cell(R, C, V1) :-
    orientation_is_column,
    n_rows(Nr), n_cols(Nc),
    K = (C - BC1) / ((BC2 - BC1) + 2),
    K >= 0,
    C = BC1 + K * ((BC2 - BC1) + 2),
    C < Nc.

output_cell(R, C, V1) :-
    orientation_is_row,
    n_rows(Nr), n_cols(Nc),
    K = (R - BR1) / ((BR2 - BR1) + 2),
    K >= 0,
    R = BR1 + K * ((BR2 - BR1) + 2),
    R < Nr.

% Output cell for second non‑zero value (V2)
output_cell(R, C, V2) :-
    orientation_is_column,
    n_rows(Nr), n_cols(Nc),
    K = (C - BC2) / ((BC2 - BC1) + 2),
    K >= 0,
    C = BC2 + K * ((BC2 - BC1) + 2),
    C < Nc.

output_cell(R, C, V2) :-
    orientation_is_row,
    n_rows(Nr), n_cols(Nc),
    K = (R - BR2) / ((BR2 - BR1) + 2),
    K >= 0,
    R = BR2 + K * ((BR2 - BR1) + 2),
    R < Nr.

% Output cell for zero (only when neither V1 nor V2 applies)
output_cell(R, C, 0) :-
    orientation_is_column,
    n_rows(Nr), n_cols(Nc),
    not(output_cell(R, C, V1)),
    not(output_cell(R, C, V2)).

output_cell(R, C, 0) :-
    orientation_is_row,
    n_rows(Nr), n_cols(Nc),
    not(output_cell(R, C, V1)),
    not(output_cell(R, C, V2)).

% Link to output predicate
output(R, C, Color) :- output_cell(R, C, Color).

% Exactly one answer set
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(C) } 1 :- true.

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

outside(R2, C2) :-
